title: A single RPC hiccup during a Flashbots bundle wait crashes the whole bot: the library throws inside an async block listener, ethers does not catch it, and src has no unhandledRejection handler

evidence.note: await bundle.wait() on every ETH private attempt (snipe buys, deliberate private buys, private sells, partial sells)

waitForBundleInclusion registers an async handler on the provider "block" event; it awaits getTransactionCount (:375) and getBlock(target) (:385) and throws "Unable to get block" when getBlock returns null (:386-387); any rejection of those calls also escapes the handler
emit calls listener.call(...) inside try/catch, which only catches synchronous throws; the promise an async listener returns is dropped, so its rejection is unhandled
no output: Node 22 default (--unhandled-rejections=throw) ends the process (the RC-05 policy entry is AUD-BUY-005)

evidence.ref: node fb-wait-repro.js (Node 22.16.0, scratch folder outside the repo; real @flashbots/ethers-provider-bundle@1.0.0 waitForBundleInclusion on an ethers@6.16.0 AbstractProvider subclass whose _perform answers locally; no src/ import, no SQLite, no .env, no network)
evidence.note: without a handler the process printed "Error: Unable to get block: 101 at LocalProvider.handler (...ethers-provider-bundle/build/index.js:387:31)" and exited with code 1; with process.on("unhandledRejection") added it printed "unhandledRejection caught: Unable to get block: 101" and "process still alive", exit 0

sibling_sites_checked: The library's waitForTxInclusion (:428-470) has the same async-listener shape but is unused (no sendPrivateTransaction caller). Passthrough and bloXroute do not use the library wait. ethers TransactionResponse.wait() catches errors inside its own listeners (provider.js:1196-1206). Every other async listener or un-awaited call in src is the RC-05 policy entry AUD-BUY-005; this entry is the concrete trigger inside the TX slice.
severity_rationale: S1: the condition is ordinary, one transient RPC error, a rate limit, or a load-balanced node that has not yet seen the block the event came from, during the ~12 s each ETH attempt spends in bundle.wait(); the consequence is the whole bot process exiting, taking every exit monitor and anti-rug subscription down until the operator notices and restarts. If the crash happens mid-buy the bundle can still land with no trade row (AUD-BUY-002 class). Reproduced with the real library on Node 22.16.0.
recommendation: Phase 24: do not depend on the library's event-based wait. Replace bundle.wait() with the slice's own bounded receipt+nonce reconcile (reconcileInclusion already exists) or wrap it so no listener rejection can escape; and decide the process-wide unhandledRejection policy on card OD-6 (RC-05). Prove it in Phase 23 with a provider that returns null for the target block.

triage.note: Reproduced as a real process death (plan 23-12): fixtures/bundleWaitCrash.ts runs as a railed child, loads src/main and src/bot, builds the context with the real buildChainRegistry and createChainContext and calls the real FlashbotsMevStrategy.sendTransaction (relayUrl on a loopback relay, the inert FLASHBOTS_AUTH_KEY sentinel, a plain transfer, ctx.wallet, ctx.httpProvider, maxRetries 1); the strategy simulates, sends the library bundle and its raw builders fanout and reaches its own bundle.wait(). Block 101 is mined with the transaction 2 s after the first eth_sendBundle and block 102 one slot later; the first eth_getBlockByNumber(101) answers null, as a load-balanced node whose backend has not yet seen the block does (AC-48). The process exits with code 1 and stderr 'Error: Unable to get block: 101' about 4 to 8 s after the send (claim bundle-wait-null-block-exits). Healthy control (block answered) survives and sendTransaction returns the broadcast hash. Contained (process handlers first): the process survives and the work settles, because the library's handler stays registered after its throw, runs again on block 102, gets block 101 and resolves included; so a process-level handler alone recovers this wait on the next block. Phase 24 reading: replacing bundle.wait() with the slice's own bounded receipt+nonce reconcile, or wrapping it so no listener rejection escapes (card OD-6), flips the claim to looks fixed (shown by a fix-shaped mutation that flips only this claim); so does a process-level unhandledRejection handler installed when src/main or src/bot loads; a handler installed only inside runMain or startMultiChainBot is out of reach, so the proof stays failing rather than reporting a false fix.
